recommendations.regimenLabel: High-dose corticosteroid for acute disabling relapse
steps: Acute disabling relapse: high-dose corticosteroids (IV/oral methylprednisolone ~3–5 days).
Plasma exchange for severe steroid-refractory relapse.
Disease-modifying therapy decided by neurology (relapse rate/MRI activity).
Symptomatic care (spasticity, bladder, fatigue) and rehabilitation.

drugRefs.dose: 500 mg–1 g once daily for 3–5 days
drugRefs.why: Shortens the duration of an acute disabling relapse; exclude infection (pseudo-relapse) first. Disease-modifying therapy is selected separately by neurology.

refs: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 22e — Multiple Sclerosis and Other Demyelinating Diseases
ABN Guidelines on the Use of Disease-Modifying Therapies in Multiple Sclerosis
2017 Revised McDonald Diagnostic Criteria for Multiple Sclerosis

decision.label: High-dose steroids for disabling relapse; exclude pseudo-relapse

confirm: Neurological symptoms disseminated in time and space in a young adult; MRI white-matter lesions, oligoclonal bands. Confirm relapse vs pseudo-relapse (exclude infection/heat).
